### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via bindAppArtifactHandlers (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4bcced0b451ecffd56689229e7d9842f5738a0b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1fecc564b345001df055f3a47da06642e8998440` — the merge of head `a14895b7178ae756b2892ac8e79362dfd6416e30` into base `e4bcced0b451ecffd56689229e7d9842f5738a0b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1fecc564b345001df055f3a47da06642e8998440 && git checkout 1fecc564b345001df055f3a47da06642e8998440
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e4bcced0b451ecffd56689229e7d9842f5738a0b a14895b7178ae756b2892ac8e79362dfd6416e30 && git checkout -B drift-repro e4bcced0b451ecffd56689229e7d9842f5738a0b && git merge --no-ff a14895b7178ae756b2892ac8e79362dfd6416e30

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e4bcced0b451ecffd56689229e7d9842f5738a0b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e4bcced0b451ecffd56689229e7d9842f5738a0b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK (patch round 1: the closing keyword only)

`domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_01SYEJqDL3NXxrJRBVqaMu9T` · 2026-10-18T15:22Z · on head `a14895b71` · #24289 (claim `6250629067`, report `6251604887`). This is the seat's own review at the default tier (`Clause-②: no`), read against GitHub, not the report.

**The code is accepted as it stands:**
- `withInProcessHookTitle` hands an inline `handler` the one `buildTitleSurface` the sandboxed body uses, so no second title implementation exists.
- The hook context is wrapped in a view:
  - reads go through `Reflect.get(target, prop)`, so getters keep the real context as `this`;
  - there is no `set` trap, so `ctx.input` / `ctx.result` writes land on the engine's own object;
  - the engine's context object is never mutated.
- `bindAppArtifactHandlers` wraps a copy of each function handler, so the app's declaration is not rewritten.
- `packages/objectql` and `packages/spec` are untouched; the binder option was measured as needing two opts types, one of them a spec contract.
- The A3 reproduction and the ablation went red on the in-process door only, as predicted.
- Evidence: runtime `--project local` passed 420 files / 6608 tests, and verify passed 42 files / 364 tests.
- `Clause-②: no` holds: `withInProcessHookTitle` is absent from `dist/index.d.ts`, and `HookContext` gains no member.

**Owed in this PR: the closing keyword.**
- Your own out-of-scope finding (class a, measured on a scratch run) is a member of this card's family. A hook whose `handler` NAMES a function runs in-process without `ctx.title`: `runtimeModule` with a string `handler` on the artifact door, and `functions` with a handler name on a source boot. That covers the deprecated string form, and what `objectstack build` ships for a callable it could not lower.
- The card's Expected is "the in-process hook path that `bootStack` uses gives hooks the same `ctx.title` the served runtime gives them", so this PR delivers part of it.
- By the family rule (one card covers every site of a family; no single-point card), #24289 stays open for that residual.
- Ask:
  - make the PR body's first line `Part of #24289`, with no closing keyword anywhere;
  - in the Acceptance notes, name the named-function path as the card's remaining slice, with its measured route: one `bindHooksToEngine` option, plus the `IObjectQLEngine.bindHooks` opts type (`packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts`) and `ObjectQL.bindHooks` opts (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`), which makes it a cross-lane slice;
  - no code change.

**Settled:**
- `HookContext` declares no `title` (TS2339 under `--strict` for an annotated handler). Declaring it is a published-type change in the spec lane. As the dev suggests, it is sequenced after the named-function slice so the declaration does not run ahead of what the runtime delivers. The seat carries it in the card's release note; it is not filed separately.
- Before pushing, read this head's checks and fold any red into the same round.

   - Locally: 63 derived families exit 0, with 0 NOT-MEASURED. The 10 declared-wide families covering `packages/runtime` and `packages/verify` exit 0, `check:init-service-contract` among them. eslint exits 0. runtime `--project local` passed 420 files / 6608 tests; verify passed 42 files / 364 tests.
   - CI on this head at this stamp: no failure; `Test Core` is running. ⛔ Not ready until every check on the head is green.
5. **Deviations accepted:**
   - the runtime-side wrap instead of a binder option (measured: an option needs two opts types, one of them in the spec contract);
   - one `main` merge;
